_about: Frozen Phase 2 recipe. Every production asset is generated from this, via recipe.py. Change it only through a new bake-off.

generator._weight_dtype_note: bf16 ('default') was tested and rejected: at 1536 px it spills past 16 GB VRAM and the varying offload makes runs non-reproducible (mean pixel diff ~22 between identical runs), a variation as large as any bf16-vs-fp8 difference. fp8 at 1536 is pixel-identical run to run.

prompt.style: soft children's picture book illustration, smooth matte clay toy look, rounded chunky friendly shapes, warm bright colours, gentle soft shading, no outlines
prompt.sprite_template: {subject}, 2D top-down video game sprite, {style}, centred on a plain white background

variants._about: Recolours and finish edits of an already-chosen asset, so silhouettes stay identical.

ground._about: Not generated: flat procedural fills (postprocess.flat_fill — wrap-around blotch noise, no direction, so no banding), colours sampled from the style anchor. Summed sine waves were tried first and showed diagonal banding. See tools/comfy/ground_check.py.

selection._about: Quality over speed: every asset is generated from several seeds and the best is picked and pinned in asset_manifest.json.

prompt_lessons: Describe what a prop LOOKS LIKE from above ('a round bush viewed from straight above, puffy leaf clusters, flat lay'); 'seen from directly above' alone yields side views.
'pointing straight up, perfectly symmetrical' gets true top-down cars, but facing is unreliable: record facing per asset and rotate in post.

Judge a car's facing by its windscreen and headlights, never by light colour: B2's amber lights are TAIL lights, and recording it 'up' made every car drive backwards. Edit instructions must name the real end ('the back of the car, the top of the picture').
Reproducibility verified: the frozen recipe regenerates a probe pixel-identically (max diff 0), so a pinned seed fully defines an asset.
Never use the full style frame as the Redux reference: it leaks the track into every asset. Use the object-only style board.
At 1536 px the board pulls in extra objects unless the lock is light (factor >= 4.5, weight <= 0.75).
FLUX cannot make tileable ground ('a picture of a tile'); the style's ground is flat colour anyway, so it is procedural.
